name: Iidabashi
tagline: Otemachi in 6 minutes and Tokyo in 12 minutes. Served by 5 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥130,000 to ¥140,000.
summary: The station is in Chiyoda City, where JR East, Tokyo Metro and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 5 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 6 minutes to Otemachi, 15 minutes to Shinjuku, 21 minutes to Shibuya and 27 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. The station stands 5.2 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 11.6 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 5.2 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 4.3 m to 15.9 m, a difference of 11.6 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 3 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 3 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 16 clinics and 15 pharmacies. The nearest facility recorded as a hospital is 日本歯科大学附属病院, about 232 m from the station. The next nearest is JCHO東京新宿メディカルセンター, about 278 m away. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 5 lines serve the station. JR Chuo-Sobu Line (Local) run through it. Tokyo Metro Tozai Line also call here. Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line are available too. Tokyo Metro Namboku Line and Toei Oedo Line stop here as well. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 1 line, Tokyo Metro runs 3 lines and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Tozai Line runs at 160% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 木場→門前仲町, which this station is not on. Tokyo Metro Namboku Line runs at 156%. Its busiest stretch is 駒込→本駒込, which this station is likewise not on. Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line runs at 153%. Its busiest stretch is 東池袋→護国寺, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: One room ¥130,000 to ¥140,000, 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000, 1LDK ¥220,000 to ¥230,000 and 2LDK ¥350,000 to ¥360,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Ushigome-Kagurazaka, but Iidabashi is ahead on the number of lines and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: 814 m away in a straight line. It takes 7 minutes longer to reach Otemachi than Iidabashi. One-room rents run about ¥17,000 lower.

neighbours.lead: Suidobashi is ahead on the number of medical facilities, but Iidabashi is ahead on the number of lines.
neighbours.note: 909 m away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Iidabashi.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want another route when a line stops
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
noiseSources: The 首都高速5号池袋線 viaduct runs 117 m away. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
外堀通り (3 lanes each way) runs 40 m away, right beside the station. Traffic on it never stops

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 11 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: Among the 23 wards' stations, comparatively few of the points around this one fall inside the projected inundation area for the largest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 5 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
